meta.dataNotes: REAL research-stage data from a FOCUSED web screen of selected NSE small-caps (not an exhaustive 251+ universe scan). Figures are point-in-time snapshots from authorised aggregators (Screener/Trendlyne/MoneyWorks4Me/MarketsMojo) on the dates in each 'sources' entry, gathered early-to-mid June 2026; they LAG live quotes and MUST be re-verified on NSE/BSE before any decision. Fundamental fields are well-sourced; several technical fields (exact 50/200-DMA, RSI) are best-estimates pending the Yahoo/GitHub-Actions refresh. Surveillance flags set false were not individually confirmed for every name in search results — verify on the NSE ASM/GSM report. Not financial advice.
meta.amfiCutoffNote: AMFI Jan 2026 reference: large = top 100 (floor ~Rs 1,05,000 cr), mid = ranks 101-250 (floor ~Rs 34,700 cr), small/micro = 251+ (below ~Rs 34,700 cr). All included names sit below the mid-cap floor. Re-verify against the live AMFI list.

thesis.core: Vertically integrated generics maker (US/UK/Australia OTC + Rx) with in-house CRAMS/CMO capacity; consistent debt-free, high-ROCE compounding with USFDA approvals widening the product basket.
thesis.catalysts: New USFDA ANDA approvals (e.g. Benzonatate, Apr 2026), UK/EU capacity ramp, possible buyback; PAT +64% YoY in Q4 FY26.
thesis.whatMustGoRight: Approval cadence sustains, margins hold as generics price-erode, and CMO utilisation rises without a leveraged acquisition.
thesis.risks: US generic price erosion, regulatory/USFDA inspection risk, FX, customer concentration in OTC.
thesis.invalidation: An adverse USFDA action (warning letter/import alert), OPM contraction >300bps for two quarters, debt-funded M&A pushing D/E above 0.5, or a decisive close below the 200-DMA.

thesis.core: Indigenisation of defence (batteries, e-fuzes) and railway safety (Kavach/TCAS) — a small-cap with a rising order book where each large win moves earnings materially; near debt-free with 27% ROCE.
thesis.catalysts: Kavach order finalisations across zones, defence battery/spin-off orders, export wins; Q2 FY26 PAT +170%.
thesis.whatMustGoRight: Kavach tenders convert to executed revenue on schedule and rich valuation (P/E ~45) is supported by sustained 30%+ earnings growth.
thesis.risks: Lumpy government ordering, valuation de-rating risk (already corrected ~21% in 6m), working-capital build, execution.
thesis.invalidation: Order book stalling for 2+ quarters, OCF turning negative, any promoter pledge appearing, or entry into ASM/GSM.

thesis.core: Domestic No.2 in industrial coding & marking (CIJ/TIJ/laser printers) on a razor-and-blade model — printers seed a high-margin annuity of inks/consumables; debt-free, ROE ~28%, trading at a deep P/E discount (~10x) to peers.
thesis.catalysts: Manufacturing/PLI-led demand for coding on packaging, consumables annuity compounding, market-share gains via import substitution; valuation re-rating optionality.
thesis.whatMustGoRight: Installed base keeps expanding so consumables revenue compounds, and the market eventually re-rates a high-quality, cheap compounder.
thesis.risks: Lower liquidity (smaller float — confirm exitability), slower top-line growth than peers, competition from MNCs.
thesis.invalidation: ROE falling below 18%, consumables mix shrinking, any debt build, or 30-session traded value sustaining below the Rs 1 cr liquidity floor.

thesis.core: Debt-free, cash-rich exporter pivoting to the structural lab-grown-diamond (LGD) shift, now building a domestic LGD retail brand (ORIGEM) funded by a Rs 202 cr QIP — optionality on a new high-growth consumer category.
thesis.catalysts: ORIGEM store rollout (toward ~200 stores), LGD penetration of bridal/fashion jewellery, US export recovery.
thesis.whatMustGoRight: ORIGEM scales profitably without eroding the cash balance, and LGD price deflation is offset by volume.
thesis.risks: LGD price deflation, retail-expansion cash burn (rising working capital), US tariff/demand cyclicality, ROE diluted by the large cash pile and QIP.
thesis.invalidation: ORIGEM losses persisting beyond ~2 years, OCF turning negative, ROCE falling below 15%, or LGD realisations collapsing.

thesis.core: Debt-free, cash-rich seamless-pipe leader (DP Jindal group) leveraged to oil-&-gas and infrastructure capex; cheap (P/E ~12, P/B ~1.5) with capacity to ride a domestic capex up-cycle.
thesis.catalysts: Oil-&-gas/water pipeline capex, import-substitution in seamless tubes, capacity additions; cyclical earnings upswing.
thesis.whatMustGoRight: Demand cycle stays firm and realisations hold; the cash-heavy balance sheet gets deployed productively.
thesis.risks: Cyclical end-markets (oil & gas), steel-price and spread volatility, modest ROE — more value/cyclical than a structural compounder.
thesis.invalidation: Sustained capacity under-utilisation, ROCE falling below 12%, a down-cycle in seamless realisations, or large value-destructive capex.

thesis.core: Integrated water-treatment play (engineering + chemicals + consumer) levered to India's water/wastewater capex (Jal Jeevan, industrial reuse) — a structural theme, currently beaten down and on the watchlist for a technical turn.
thesis.catalysts: Large EPC water order wins, recycling/reuse mandates, BOOT project monetisation; mean-reversion after a ~38% one-year drawdown.
thesis.whatMustGoRight: Order execution lifts the thin (~10%) margins, working capital normalises, and the downtrend bottoms.
thesis.risks: Low promoter holding (~25.5%), lumpy EPC margins, rising working capital, and a firmly negative price trend (below 50- & 200-DMA, near 52-wk low).
thesis.invalidation: WATCH only until it reclaims the 200-DMA on volume. Abandon if OCF turns negative, an order-book stall appears, or promoter holding falls further.
